subject: Latency anomaly — account impact summary & action playbook
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@speedbank.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: SpeedBank Ops <ops@speedbank.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 23:17:00 -0800
Subject: High latency spike observed tonight (Dec 10)

Diego,

We saw a sudden latency spike across several inference routes between 22:40 and 23:05 PST tonight. Impacted paths: text-generation v3 and embeddings-v1. Roughly 30% increase in 95th percentile for our production traffic; some batches timed out and we had to fallback to a smaller model which caused functional regressions in our chat flow.

Can you confirm if Redwood had any incidents on your side? We need an initial RCA and a timeline — our compliance team is asking for a short summary and any mitigations you applied.

Thanks,
Anita
Anita Shah
Head of Platform Reliability
SpeedBank

---
Attachment: client-sample-logs.txt (log excerpt)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@speedbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 00:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency spike observed tonight (Dec 10)

Anita — thanks for the alert and the log excerpt. We're looking into this now and will prioritize a brief response for your compliance team.

Quick notes from initial triage (preliminary):
- We observed elevated token-generation latency on the serving cluster in us-west-2 for models matching text-generation-v3 slices between 22:35–23:10 PST.
- Autoscaling delayed due to an unusually high number of simultaneous long-lived KV cache loads; this produced transient queueing on the GPU proxy.
- No failed deployments or config rollouts were in progress at the time.

Immediate mitigations we applied (11 Dec 00:02 PST):
1) Manually increased burst capacity on the affected pool to drain queued requests.
2) Applied a temporary routing policy to divert non-critical traffic to a dedicated lower-cost pool.
3) Flushed a subset of stale prefix caches that were contributing to long load times.

We're collecting a full timeline and will send a formal RCA with attachments tomorrow (Dec 12). Would you like that as a PDF and a CSV timeline? Also proposing a 30-minute verification call on Monday (Dec 14) to walk through the checklist.

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Technical Account Lead — Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@speedbank.com>, SpeedBank Ops <ops@speedbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident summary, timeline, and verification playbook (Dec 10 latency anomaly)

Anita and SpeedBank team —

Please find the post-incident package below. This is a concise executive RCA, the chronological timeline we reconstructed, and a short verification playbook for your engineers to run against your integration.

Executive summary (short):
- What happened: A latency anomaly affected select model-serving routes (text-generation-v3, embeddings-v1) on our us-west-2 serving pool on Dec 10, 22:35–23:10 PST. The root cause was a combination of (a) an unusual surge of concurrent KV cache population requests triggered by a rare request pattern from a subset of customers and (b) the autoscale policy delay for the dedicated pool due to a mismatched scaling signal threshold.
- Impact: SpeedBank experienced elevated 95th percentile latency (~30% increase) and several timeouts that caused your application to fallback to a smaller model. No data leakage was detected.
- Immediate mitigations: manual burst expansion, temporary routing to alternate pool, targeted cache eviction.
- Long-term fixes planned and committed (below).

Attachments included: root-cause-summary.pdf (detailed RCA), latency-timeline.csv (per-minute metrics for affected routes), verification-playbook.md (actions for your team).

Timeline (reconstructed):
- 22:34 PST — first elevated queue depths observed in metrics for pool gw-usw2-02.
- 22:35–22:43 PST — 95th/99th latency climbs as KV cache warm-up loads spike; autoscaler observed high load but did not trigger immediate capacity due to smoothing window.
- 22:43 PST — client retries increase; some requests time out at the proxy layer.
- 22:45 PST — SpeedBank Ops reports user-facing latency (email received 23:17).
- 22:50 PST — internal alerting threshold breached; secondary on-call paged.
- 22:52 PST — manual burst capacity applied.
- 23:00 PST — routing policy adjusted to divert non-critical traffic.
- 23:06 PST — latency returns to baseline.

Action items and deliverables (committed dates):
1) Autoscale tuning change — reduce smoothing window and add a KV-load signal to trigger earlier (ETA: 2027-01-05). Owner: Runtime Infra (RED-4129).
2) Prefix/KV cache heuristics — add per-customer parallelization guard to avoid synchronized large loads (ETA: 2027-01-12). Owner: Serving Runtime.
3) Enhanced customer-facing thresholds — allow customer-configurable routing thresholds so accounts with critical SLAs can opt into faster burst scaling (ETA: 2027-02-01). Owner: Product.
4) Post-deploy verification tests — new synthetic workload to exercise rare request patterns in pre-prod (ETA: 2027-01-20). Owner: QA.

Verification playbook (short steps for SpeedBank):
- Step 1: Pull the attached latency-timeline.csv and verify the per-minute spikes align with your own ingest logs.
- Step 2: Run the provided verification-playbook.md (attached) in a staging account to reproduce the pattern; we can run a guided session with you.
- Step 3: Confirm acceptance criteria: baseline 95th percentile under 1200ms for your traffic slices and no timed-out batches under synthetic load.

Open items:
- We will schedule a joint verification session. Proposed window: Mon, Dec 14 10:00–10:30 PST. Please confirm.
- Credit/compensation: Marissa (cc'd) will follow up with a credits proposal if you request.

I am attaching the artifacts and linking the internal ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RED-4129 (autscale tuning) and the postmortem doc on Drive.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Technical Account Lead — Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
